title: B-tree lookup on 100M rows: 4 page reads instead of 1M
caption: Each level narrows the key range about 500-fold; the top levels stay in memory, so usually only the leaf and heap page hit disk.

steps.text: 1. Start at the root page. It holds ~500 separator keys, each pointing to a child that covers ~200k keys.
2. Binary-search the keys and follow the child whose range contains 42. That internal page splits its range again into ~400-key leaves.
3. Repeat until a leaf page, which stores the key and a pointer (page, slot) to the row in the heap.
4. Read that one heap page. Three index levels (log₅₀₀(100M) ≈ 3) plus the heap page = 4 reads, against ~1M pages for a sequential scan.
